sentences.text: This appeal coming on for order this day, the court passed the following:

ORDER The appellant / Oriental Insurance Company Limited (non- appellant No.3 before the Tribunal) has filed the present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 against the award dated 26.05.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Neemuch in Claim Case No.27/2018,
whereby the compensation of Rs.10,01,500/- has been awarded in favour of respondent No.1 /
claimant.
So far as Insurance Company is concerned, out of Rs.10,01,354/- only Rs.1,00,000/- has been awarded and Rs.9,01,500/- has been passed against non-appellant No.1, 2 & 4 (before the Tribunal).
02. According to the claimant on 30.08.2011, near about 3:30 pm, he was driving the motorcycle and going to Neemuch.

Non-appellant No.1 came on his motorcycle bearing registration No.MP 44 MA 8328 rashly and negligently from the wrong side and dashed him, due to which is suffered frontal bone fracture on his head, fracture of jaw bones and various other injuries on other parts of the face.
He was treated in the hospital at Neemuch, Udaypur and Ahmedabad.
He suffered disfiguration, loss of memory etc.
He was 30 years of age at the time of accident and used to earn Rs.1,60,523/- per annum.
The vehicle was driven and owned by non-appellants No.1 & 2 and the same was insured by non-appellant No.3.
Non-appellant No.4 has been impleaded as he recently purchased the vehicle.
After examining the evidence came on record, the learned Tribunal assessed the compensation of Rs.10,01,354/- payable by the non-appellants.

According to the Tribunal as per the contract of the insurance, the limit of compensation payable by the Insurance Company is only Rs.1,00,000/-, therefore, out of Rs.10,01,500/-, , Rs.1,00,000/- has been awarded against the Insurance Company and Rs.9,01,500/- against other non-appellants.
Hence, the present appeal is before this Court.
03. According to the appellant, the Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- against the Insurance Company.
The injured was an insured person and does not come under the definition third party.
The award is liable to be set aside as Section 165 of the Motor Vehicle Act clearly says that only third party can claim compensation.
The injured himself was negligent in driving the motorcycle, he was not having the valid and effective license and the motorcycle was not insured with the Insurance Company.
The claimant has wrongly impleaded the Insurance Company of his own motorcycle and liability is only limited to Rs.1,00,000/-.
The injured suffered eye loss and loss of sense of smell.

04. Learned counsel for the respondent / claimant has placed reliance upon a judgment delivered by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s Ashalata Bhowmik & Others reported in 2018 (4) ACCD 1909 (SC), whereby the compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- has been awarded as the deceased himself dashed the motorcycle on a tree.
